name: E minor
commonMistakes: Pressing too hard causes finger fatigue fast
Letting the 1st finger touch the high E string and mute it
audioNote: Low, dark, easy first chord — only 2 fingers needed.

name: A minor
commonMistakes: Muting the high E string with the ring finger
Strumming the low E string (should stay open, not muted, but many beginners over-mute)
audioNote: One of the most common minor chords in beginner songs.

name: C major
commonMistakes: Strumming the low E string (must be muted/skipped)
Buzzing on the B string because the 1st finger isn't close enough to the fret
audioNote: Bright, common — the classic 'muted low string' beginner trap.

name: G major
commonMistakes: Buzzing on the high strings from not enough finger arch
Slow transitions from G to C or D at first

beginnerVariant.label: 3-finger G (skip pinky, easier but less full)

audioNote: Full, ringing chord — used in a huge share of beginner songs.

name: D major
commonMistakes: Strumming the low E or A string by accident
Fingers overlapping and muting the high E string
audioNote: Small triangular shape near the top of the neck.

name: A major
commonMistakes: Three fingers crowded on one fret causing accidental muting
Strumming the low E string
audioNote: Bright major chord, tricky finger crowding for beginners.

name: E major
commonMistakes: Muting the G string with the 1st finger
audioNote: Big, full, all six strings ring.

name: F major (barre)
commonMistakes: Not enough thumb-behind-neck pressure so strings buzz
Barre finger rolled flat instead of using the side of the finger
audioNote: The classic first barre chord — needs hand strength, practice daily in short bursts.

name: G dominant 7th
commonMistakes: Confusing with G major
audioNote: Bluesy pull toward C — common turnaround chord.

name: A minor 7th
commonMistakes: Easy chord — mainly a smoother substitute for Am
audioNote: Mellow, jazzy, only 2 fingers.

name: D suspended 2
commonMistakes: Forgetting to lift off the high E finger from the D chord shape
audioNote: Open, floaty sound — great strum-pattern color chord.

name: C add 9
commonMistakes: Stretch to the pinky on the high E string can feel awkward at first
audioNote: Sparkly, popular in acoustic pop songs as a C substitute.

name: E5 power chord
commonMistakes: Letting the muted strings ring by accident
audioNote: No major/minor quality — just root + fifth. Rock staple, moves easily up the neck.

name: B-flat major (barre)
commonMistakes: Same barre-pressure issues as F, plus root on the A string is easy to miss
audioNote: Movable A-shape barre chord — once F is comfortable, this is the same shape moved up.

commonMistakes: Barre finger not pressing evenly across every string — roll toward the side of the finger, not flat
Not enough thumb-behind-neck support, causing buzz
audioNote: Movable A-shape barre chord, barred at fret 3.
